chunks: Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about going out once the month of Ramadan has begun.

He عليه السلام said: "No, except in matters about which I inform you: going out to Mecca, or military campaign in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or wealth whose loss you fear, or a brother whose destruction you fear, and he is not a brother from the same father and mother."

key_terms.أَخٌ: a brother, here meaning a fellow believer rather than a full sibling
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time of obligatory sawm
key_terms.فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: in the way of Allah, for a religiously sanctioned cause
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth that one fears may perish
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, a valid destination excepted from the ruling
key_terms.هَلَاكَهُ: his or its destruction or perishing

ai.seo_question: When is travel allowed after the month of Ramadan has begun?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the disliked nature of travel after the beginning of Ramadan, while identifying specific exceptions. The exceptions include travel for Mecca, jihad, protecting vulnerable property, and aiding a brother facing destruction, with the final phrase clarifying that this refers to a non-blood brother.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1968 - Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
"I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about traveling once the Month of Ramadan has begun.

Imam (as) said: 'Do not [travel], except in cases I will inform you of: traveling to Mecca, waging battle in the way of Allah (swt) Almighty, preserving wealth you fear will perish, or saving a brother you fear will face destruction—and he is not a brother from the same father and mother.'"
